title: The God of Mercy Be Ador'd
description: The God of Mercy Be Ador'd in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book III, prepared for the Lord's Supper, hymn 30, headed “2d. C. M”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The God of mer-cy be a-dor'd, Who calls our souls from death, Who saves by his re-deem-ing word, And new cre-a-ting breath.

lines: The God of mercy be ador'd,
Who calls our souls from death,
Who saves by his redeeming word,
To praise the Father and the Son
The One in Three, and Three in One,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
